input.question: Has the addition of "Drink Responsibly" or "Winners know when to quit" in advertisements actually made any change to alcoholic and gambling addictions?
input.ground_truth: Personally, I don't know any of the statistics. But, I always thought such slogans were more to relive the companies from legal action. Like they could say "Look, we TOLD them to drink responsibly, it isn't our fault he had 20 of our beers and drove".

Question: Has the addition of "Drink Responsibly" or "Winners know when to quit" in advertisements actually made any change to alcoholic and gambling addictions?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of cookies. On the box, there is a sticker that says, “Eat only a little, too many can make you sick.” 

Now, some grown-ups think that if they see that sticker, they will eat fewer cookies. But sometimes, they still eat lots of cookies because they really want to.

It’s kind of the same with the words like “Drink Responsibly” on beer or wine bottles, or “Winners know when to quit” on gambling ads. Some people might remember the message and try to drink or gamble less. But for others, the message doesn’t really change what they do—they might still drink a lot or keep gambling.

So, the words on the ads are trying to help people be careful, but it’s not always enough to stop someone who is having a hard time with too much drinking or gambling.
